## Description

Implement a lockless histogram using atomics, and use a sync.Map for attribute access.  This improves performance by ~2x.

The design is very similar to https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/pull/7427, but with one additional change to make the histogram data point itself atomic:

* For cumulative histograms, which do not use a hot/cold limitedSyncMap, we use a hot/cold data point.  This way, we maintain the keys in the sync map, but still ensure that collection gets a consistent view of measure() calls.

## Description

This improves the concurrent performance of the histogram reservoir's Offer function by 4x (i.e. 75% reduction).

Accomplish this by locking each measurement, rather than locking around the entire storage.  Also, defer extracting the trace context from context.Context until collection time. This improves the performance of Offer, which is on the measure hot path.  Exemplars are often overwritten, so deferring the operation until Collect reduces the overall work.

```

                           │   main.txt   │              hist.txt              │

                           │    sec/op    │   sec/op     vs base               │

FixedSizeReservoirOffer-24    211.4n ± 3%   177.5n ± 3%  -16.04% (p=0.002 n=6)

HistogramReservoirOffer-24   200.85n ± 2%   47.41n ± 2%  -76.40% (p=0.002 n=6)

geomean                       206.1n        91.73n       -55.48%

```

## Description

Implement a lockless histogram using atomics, and use a sync.Map for attribute access.  This improves performance by ~2x.

The design is very similar to https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/pull/7427, but with one additional change to make the histogram data point itself atomic:

* For cumulative histograms, which do not use a hot/cold limitedSyncMap, we use a hot/cold data point.  This way, we maintain the keys in the sync map, but still ensure that collection gets a consistent view of measure() calls.

Parallel benchmarks:

```

geomean                                                                  274.3n        128.8n       -53.05%

```

zero memory allocations before and after this change for Measure().  Omitted for brevity

I figured out why the benchmark results were so poor: The benchmark was recording all observations in a single bucket, and each bucket has its own lock, so there were effectively no parallelism gains.  I switched the benchmark to record observations in different buckets, and that shows that this is a ~70% performance improvement when exemplars are being recorded.

## Description

Implement a lockless histogram using atomics, and use a sync.Map for attribute access.  This improves performance by ~2x.

The design is very similar to https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/pull/7427, but with one additional change to make the histogram data point itself atomic:

* For cumulative histograms, which do not use a hot/cold limitedSyncMap, we use a hot/cold data point.  This way, we maintain the keys in the sync map, but still ensure that collection gets a consistent view of measure() calls.

```

zero memory allocations before and after this change for Measure().  Omitted for brevity

## Description

This improves the concurrent performance of the histogram reservoir's Offer function by 4x (i.e. 75% reduction).

Accomplish this by locking each measurement, rather than locking around the entire storage.  Also, defer extracting the trace context from context.Context until collection time. This improves the performance of Offer, which is on the measure hot path.  Exemplars are often overwritten, so deferring the operation until Collect reduces the overall work.

geomean                       206.1n        91.73n       -55.48%

# Pull Request: Use sync.Map and atomics to improve sum performance (open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go#7427)

**Canonical URL**: https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/pull/7427  

**Author**: dashpole  

**Created**: 2025-09-29T14:36:56Z · **Updated**: 2025-10-14T14:40:27Z  

**Collected**: 2026-07-14T14:35:41Z  

**State**: merged (2025-10-07T13:40:23Z)  

**Branch**: `optimize_counter_syncmap` → `main`  

**Changes**: +437 / -121 across 14 files  

**Labels**: area:metrics  

**Milestone**: v1.39.0

---

## Description

Alternative to https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/pull/7380

This uses a sync.Map and atomics for the sum's counter value.  This intentionally introduces a new race condition that didn't previously exist:

* It is possible for the exemplar to be recorded in the batch of metrics after the add() for cumulative sum aggregations. For cumulative, this isn't a huge issue since exemplars are expected to persist across collection cycles. This is difficult to fix because we can't manage the internal storage of an exemplar.Reservoir (to atomically swap between hot and cold storage).  If we are able to make assumptions about how exemplar reservoirs are managed (i.e. that the number of and order of exemplars returned is always the same), then we could possibly fix this by merging at export time.

### Alternatives Considered

#### RWLock for the map instead of sync.Map

This is significantly less performant.

#### Single sync.Map without hotColdWaitGroup

Deleting keys from the sync.Map concurrently with measurements (during Clear() of the sync.Map) can cause measurements to be made to a counter that has already been read, exported and deleted.  This can produce incorrect sums when delta is used.  Instead, atomically switching writes to a completely empty sync.Map and waiting for writes to the previous sync.Map complete eliminates this issue.

#### Use two sync.Map for cumulative sums

One idea I explored was doing a hot-cold swap for cumulative sums just like we do for delta sums.  We would swap the hot and cold sync.Maps, wait for writes to the cold sync.Map to complete while new writes go to the hot map.  Then, once we are done reading the cold map, we could merge the contents of the cold map back into the new hot map.

Now, when translation would drop data (e.g., invalid label/value), the exporter emits a `NewInvalidMetric`, and Prometheus scrapes **fail with HTTP 500** by default. To preserve the prior behavior (scrapes succeed while errors are logged), configure your Prometheus HTTP handler with: `promhttp.HandlerOpts{ ErrorHandling: promhttp.ContinueOnError }`. (#7363)

## Description

Implement a lockless histogram using atomics, and use a sync.Map for attribute access.  This improves performance by ~2x.

The design is very similar to https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/pull/7427, but with one additional change to make the histogram data point itself atomic:

* For cumulative histograms, which do not use a hot/cold limitedSyncMap, we use a hot/cold data point.  This way, we maintain the keys in the sync map, but still ensure that collection gets a consistent view of measure() calls.

**Labels**: —

## Description

This improves the concurrent performance of the histogram reservoir's Offer function by 4x (i.e. 75% reduction).

Accomplish this by locking each measurement, rather than locking around the entire storage.  Also, defer extracting the trace context from context.Context until collection time. This improves the performance of Offer, which is on the measure hot path.  Exemplars are often overwritten, so deferring the operation until Collect reduces the overall work.

```

```

## Overview

### Added

- Greatly reduce the cost of recording metrics in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/metric` using hashing for map keys. (#7175)

- Add `WithInstrumentationAttributeSet` option to `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/log`, `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/metric`, and `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/trace` packages. This provides a concurrent-safe and performant alternative to `WithInstrumentationAttributes` by accepting a pre-constructed `attribute.Set`. (#7287)

- Add experimental observability for the Prometheus exporter in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/exporters/prometheus`. Check the `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/exporters/prometheus/internal/x` package documentation for more information. (#7345)

- Add experimental observability metrics in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/exporters/otlp/otlplog/otlploggrpc`. (#7353)

- Add temporality selector functions `DeltaTemporalitySelector`, `CumulativeTemporalitySelector`, `LowMemoryTemporalitySelector` to `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/metric`. (#7434)

- Add experimental observability metrics for simple log processor in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/log`. (#7548)

- Add experimental observability metrics in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/exporters/otlp/otlptrace/otlptracegrpc`. (#7459)

- Add experimental observability metrics in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/exporters/otlp/otlptrace/otlptracehttp`. (#7486)

- Add experimental observability metrics for simple span processor in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/trace`. (#7374)

## Description

Implement a lockless histogram using atomics, and use a sync.Map for attribute access.  This improves performance by ~2x.

The design is very similar to https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/pull/7427, but with one additional change to make the histogram data point itself atomic:

* For cumulative histograms, which do not use a hot/cold limitedSyncMap, we use a hot/cold data point.  This way, we maintain the keys in the sync map, but still ensure that collection gets a consistent view of measure() calls.

Parallel benchmarks:

geomean                                                                  274.3n        128.8n       -53.05%

```

zero memory allocations before and after this change for Measure().  Omitted for brevity

## Overview

### Added

- Greatly reduce the cost of recording metrics in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/metric` using hashing for map keys. (#7175)

- Add `WithInstrumentationAttributeSet` option to `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/log`, `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/metric`, and `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/trace` packages. This provides a concurrent-safe and performant alternative to `WithInstrumentationAttributes` by accepting a pre-constructed `attribute.Set`. (#7287)

- Add experimental observability for the Prometheus exporter in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/exporters/prometheus`. Check the `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/exporters/prometheus/internal/x` package documentation for more information. (#7345)

- Add experimental observability metrics in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/exporters/otlp/otlplog/otlploggrpc`. (#7353)

- Add temporality selector functions `DeltaTemporalitySelector`, `CumulativeTemporalitySelector`, `LowMemoryTemporalitySelector` to `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/metric`. (#7434)

- Add experimental observability metrics for simple log processor in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/log`. (#7548)

- Add experimental observability metrics in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/exporters/otlp/otlptrace/otlptracegrpc`. (#7459)

- Add experimental observability metrics in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/exporters/otlp/otlptrace/otlptracehttp`. (#7486)

- Add experimental observability metrics for simple span processor in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/trace`. (#7374)

**Labels**: —

## Description

Implement a lockless histogram using atomics, and use a sync.Map for attribute access.  This improves performance by ~2x.

The design is very similar to https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/pull/7427, but with one additional change to make the histogram data point itself atomic:

* For cumulative histograms, which do not use a hot/cold limitedSyncMap, we use a hot/cold data point.  This way, we maintain the keys in the sync map, but still ensure that collection gets a consistent view of measure() calls.

Parallel benchmarks:

```

                                                                       │  main.txt   │              hist.txt              │

                                                                       │   sec/op    │   sec/op     vs base               │

SyncMeasure/NoView/ExemplarsDisabled/Int64Histogram/Attributes/10-24     274.5n ± 2%   125.2n ± 5%  -54.42% (p=0.002 n=6)

SyncMeasure/NoView/ExemplarsDisabled/Float64Histogram/Attributes/10-24   274.1n ± 2%   132.5n ± 2%  -51.65% (p=0.002 n=6)

geomean                                                                  274.3n        128.8n       -53.05%

```

zero memory allocations before and after this change for Measure().  Omitted for brevity

Benchmarks for collect:

```

                                                    │   main.txt    │               hist.txt               │

                                                    │    sec/op     │    sec/op     vs base                │

# Meeting Note: OpenTelemetry Go SIG — 2025-11-03

**Canonical URL**: https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/6648#issuecomment-3479584781

*   Tyler Yahn

*   David Ashpole

## Transcript

**1. otelgin Context Reversal in DataRace**

*   **Damien Mathieu** raised an issue regarding context reversal in DataRace for otelgin. The context, stored within the otelgin struct, is reverted after middleware execution to prevent parent middlewares from accessing the span. However, Go routines spawned after a request might still need the span in their context. This discussion was based on [https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go-contrib/pull/8014](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go-contrib/pull/8014).

*   Damien believes the current behavior is correct and that users should explicitly pass the current context to spawned Go routines. He cited the collector's pattern of passing context directly outside HTTP requests for processors and exporters as a good example.

*   **Tyler Yahn** agreed, suggesting that passing necessary values like the span to spawned Go routines is the appropriate solution. He also mentioned OpenTelemetry's pattern of linking spans for asynchronous operations rather than making them child references.

**2. otelgin Middleware and Temporary Multi-part Forms**

*   **Damien Mathieu** brought up an issue where using middleware causes temporary multi-part forms not to be destroyed. This occurs because the instrumentation clones the HTTP request, but the multipart form is not duplicated, preventing proper cleanup. This issue is a historical one, manifesting in otelgin but potentially affecting virtually all HTTP-related middleware.

*   References for this issue include:

    *   [https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go-contrib/issues/5946](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go-contrib/issues/5946)

    *   [https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go-contrib/pull/6609](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go-contrib/pull/6609)

**dashpole** on `sdk/metric/exemplar/storage.go` — 2025-10-03T16:12:32Z

There is still a global ordering for Offer vs Collect calls.  Consider a histogram with a single bucket.  Each Offer call that updates the atomic.Value prior to the Load() call in Collect can be considered to have happened in the previous collection interval.  Each Offer call that updates the atomic.Value after the Load() call can be considered to have happened in the next collection interval.  That principle still holds true for histograms with multiple buckets.

I don't think the complexity of hot/cold storage is necessary (at least not for histogram reservoirs)

**MrAlias** on `sdk/metric/exemplar/storage.go` — 2025-10-03T16:34:09Z

I think that works for a single bucket. But for the case of multiple buckets this could report values for subsequent buckets that occurred after a "collection cycle" for a previous bucket ended. I don't think a collection cycle is defined on a per-bucket basis, right?

**dashpole** on `sdk/metric/exemplar/storage.go` — 2025-10-03T17:34:51Z

The race that this allows is the following:

```golang

// Record a measurement in bucket A

myHist.Record(ctx, 1)

// Record a measurement in bucket B

myHist.Record(ctx, 10000)

```

In this case, it is possible for the measurement in bucket B to be included in a collection interval, but the measurement in bucket A is not included.  That would happen if we collect bucket A, then measure to buckets A and B, then collect bucket B.

A similar case exists for https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/pull/7427 as well.  Doing:

```golang

// Record a measurement with attribute set a

myCounter.Add(ctx, 1, a)

// Record a measurement with attribute set b

myCounter.Add(ctx, 10000, b)

```

The above can result in the add to attribute set `b` being included in collect, but attribute set `a` is not, since we do not globally prevent measurements during collection, and we don't iterate over attribute sets in a predictable order.

The second race (with different attribute sets) seems worse than the exemplar case, IMO, and I think both are acceptable.

**dashpole** — 2025-10-15T20:08:23Z

The other race had to do with my usage of sync.Pool.  After Collect loaded an element, that element could be placed into the sync.Pool by a subsequent store() that replaced the measurement, and then modified by another store() that retrieved it from the sync.Pool.  I worked out a way to fix this, but it made the performance around ~45ns.  In the end, I decided to just lock around each measurement, since that has the same parallel performance, is much more simple and readable, and has better single-threaded performance.

## Description

This improves the concurrent performance of the histogram reservoir's Offer function by 4x (i.e. 75% reduction).

Accomplish this by locking each measurement, rather than locking around the entire storage.  Also, defer extracting the trace context from context.Context until collection time. This improves the performance of Offer, which is on the measure hot path.  Exemplars are often overwritten, so deferring the operation until Collect reduces the overall work.

## Description

Implement a lockless histogram using atomics, and use a sync.Map for attribute access.  This improves performance by ~2x.

The design is very similar to https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/pull/7427, but with one additional change to make the histogram data point itself atomic:

* For cumulative histograms, which do not use a hot/cold limitedSyncMap, we use a hot/cold data point.  This way, we maintain the keys in the sync map, but still ensure that collection gets a consistent view of measure() calls.

## Answer: Yes — it shipped in v1.40.0, though the dataset contains no v1.40.0 release page to confirm the publish date directly.

**What the sources establish**

- **The PR** — `open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go#7474`, "Use sync.Map and atomics for fixed bucket histograms" by dashpole (`optimize_syncmap_histogram` → `main`, +560/−201 across 7 files). It implements a lockless histogram using atomics plus a sync.Map for attribute access, ~2x faster measure (−53% geomean on parallel `SyncMeasure` benchmarks, zero allocations), at the cost of ~+20% on `Collect`. **State: merged 2025-12-11T16:56:04Z. Milestone: v1.40.0.** [SRC-PR-06]
- **It missed v1.39.0.** The timeline shows it was milestoned v1.39.0 on 2025-10-16, then **demilestoned from v1.39.0 and moved to v1.40.0 on 2025-12-04**, and merged a week later. The v1.39.0 release (tag `v1.39.0`, published 2025-12-08T16:45:46Z) predates the merge, and #7474 does not appear in its changelog — only the sibling sum PR #7427 does ("Improve performance of concurrent measurements in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/metric`. (#7427)"). [SRC-PR-06], [SRC-REL-01]
- **v1.40.0 has been cut.** The `opentelemetry-go` v1.40.0 milestone (milestone/76) is **closed, 120 closed / 0 open, last updated 2026-02-02T17:59:40Z**; the contrib v1.40.0 milestone (milestone/34) is likewise closed, updated 2026-02-02T19:23:35Z. Consistent with that, the sibling PR #7443's timeline records a cross-reference from `opentelemetry-go/pull/7859` by MrAlias on 2026-02-02 — matching the pattern of the v1.39.0 release PR (#7676, cross-referenced 2025-12-05, released 2025-12-08). [SRC-MILE-03], [SRC-MILE-04], [SRC-PR-05]

**The one gap:** the dataset's only release record is v1.39.0 [SRC-REL-01]. There is no v1.40.0 release page in it, so the release's exact tag/publish timestamp and its changelog entry for #7474 cannot be quoted from these sources. The conclusion rests on the merge date + v1.40.0 milestone assignment + that milestone being closed out on 2026-02-02.

**Sources cited:** SRC-PR-06 (`opentelemetry/pulls/opentelemetry-go-7474.md`), SRC-REL-01 (`opentelemetry/releases/release-v1.39.0.md`), SRC-MILE-03 (`opentelemetry/milestones/milestone-13661613.md`), SRC-MILE-04 (`opentelemetry/milestones/milestone-14282228.md`), SRC-PR-05 (`opentelemetry/pulls/opentelemetry-go-7443.md`).

One caveat on a related source: the 2025-10-10 SIG meeting note [SRC-NOTE-03] labels "#7474" as "Exemplar reservoir optimization" and "#7443" as "Histogram optimization" — the descriptions are swapped relative to the actual PR titles, so don't rely on that note for identifying which PR is which.
